newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T up as early mark-down lures buyers.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T up as early mark-down lures buyers.

text.p: Shares in B.A.T Industries Plc were among the biggest gainers in the FTSE 100 index by late afternoon on Wednesday, after an early mark-down prompted a burst of buying in the group, dealers said.

The stock was up 6p or 0.9 percent at 577-1/2 by 1505 GMT, after earlier rising as much as 13p. Volume was active at 9.2 million shares, putting B.A.T among the top ten most actively traded UK shares.

Some said there were signs of U.S. buying following an initial retreat by B.A.T shares, sparked by a report that its Brown & Williamson unit in the U.S. had broken ranks with other tobacco firms in talks aimed at reaching a settlement of litigation over smoking-related diseases.
Press reports said B&W was concerned that a deal allowing the FDA to regulate tobacco, part of the settlement talks, could set a precedent for tobacco regulation elsewhere in the world.
"B.A.T shares fell on the U.S. dispute, some buyers came in and market-makers got caught at the wrong level," said one dealer at a major investment bank.
Separately B.A.T said today Alexander Leitch, chief executive of B.A.T's financial group which includes Allied Dunbar, Eagle Star and Threadneedle, had bought 10,791 shares at 572p.
B.A.T said it had no comment on the U.S. reports.
